title: Rapid magnetic bead nucleic acid extraction enhances influenza RT-qPCR sensitivity and subtyping success
abstract: Nucleic acid extraction remains the principal infrastructure barrier to molecular influenza testing outside centralised laboratories, since bead-based purification is normally tied to mains-powered extractors and trained operators. We evaluated SmartLid, a centrifugation-free format in which a removable magnetic key shuttles paramagnetic beads through pre-aliquoted lysis/binding, wash, and elution buffers without pipetting or powered instrumentation, against an automated magnetic-bead extractor (Nextractor NX-48S) on 311 nasopharyngeal specimens from the 2024-2025 influenza season at a National Influenza Centre. Paired eluates were amplified under identical monoplex RT-qPCR conditions for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3), and B/Victoria. Both methods gave 100% specificity (47/47 negatives; no false positives). Subtyping succeeded in 263/264 reference-positive specimens after SmartLid extraction versus 241/264 after automated extraction (99.62% versus 91.29%; difference 8.33 percentage points; discordant pairs 23 versus 1; McNemar P < 0.001). Across 240 complete pairs, cycle threshold (Ct) values were lower after SmartLid extraction (median paired difference -2.78 cycles; estimated location shift -2.60 cycles, 95% CI -2.82 to -2.37; P < 0.001) with rank-ordering of specimens conserved between methods (Spearman rho = 0.84). The advantage was preserved across all three subtypes and in both fresh and frozen specimens (adjusted P < 0.001). Specimens recovered only after SmartLid extraction had higher Ct values than dual-detected specimens (median 34.37 versus 28.54; P < 0.001), locating the gain near the assay detection limit. An instrument-free manual format can therefore exceed the extraction efficiency of an automated reference workflow, extending quality-assured influenza subtyping beyond centralised laboratories.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nucleic acid extraction remains a major barrier to decentralised molecular influenza testing because bead-based purification typically requires mains-powered extractors and trained operators, limiting access to centralised laboratories.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A comparative evaluation was conducted at a National Influenza Centre using 311 nasopharyngeal specimens collected during the 2024–2025 influenza season, comparing SmartLid, a centrifugation-free magnetic bead extraction method, against an automated magnetic-bead extractor (Nextractor NX-48S).
analysis.methods: Paired eluates from both extraction methods were amplified under identical monoplex RT-qPCR conditions for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3), and B/Victoria, with subtyping success and cycle threshold (Ct) values recorded.
analysis.main_results: SmartLid achieved 99.62% subtyping success (263/264) versus 91.29% (241/264) for the automated extractor (difference 8.33 percentage points; McNemar P < 0.001), with lower Ct values (median paired difference -2.78 cycles; estimated location shift -2.60 cycles, 95% CI -2.82 to -2.37; P < 0.001) and preserved rank-ordering (Spearman rho = 0.84).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating that an instrument-free manual extraction format can exceed the efficiency of an automated reference workflow, enabling quality-assured influenza subtyping beyond centralised laboratories.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that SmartLid could decentralise influenza molecular testing, improving access to timely subtyping and supporting surveillance and clinical decision-making in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted at a single National Influenza Centre with a specific specimen set from one season, limiting generalisability; however, the strong statistical significance and consistency across subtypes and specimen types support moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated SmartLid, an instrument-free magnetic bead extraction method, against an automated extractor for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3), and B/Victoria RT-qPCR subtyping using 311 nasopharyngeal specimens from the 2024–2025 season. SmartLid achieved higher subtyping success (99.62% vs 91.29%) and lower cycle threshold values (median difference -2.78 cycles) with preserved rank-ordering. The advantage was consistent across subtypes and specimen types. The authors conclude that SmartLid can extend quality-assured influenza subtyping beyond centralised laboratories, potentially improving decentralised testing capacity.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Nucleic acid extraction remains a major barrier to decentralised molecular influenza testing because bead-based purification typically requires mains-powered extractors and trained operators, limiting access to centralised laboratories.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A comparative evaluation was conducted at a National Influenza Centre using 311 nasopharyngeal specimens collected during the 2024–2025 influenza season, comparing SmartLid, a centrifugation-free magnetic bead extraction method, against an automated magnetic-bead extractor (Nextractor NX-48S).
elements_en.methods: Paired eluates from both extraction methods were amplified under identical monoplex RT-qPCR conditions for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3), and B/Victoria, with subtyping success and cycle threshold (Ct) values recorded.
elements_en.main_results: SmartLid achieved 99.62% subtyping success (263/264) versus 91.29% (241/264) for the automated extractor (difference 8.33 percentage points; McNemar P < 0.001), with lower Ct values (median paired difference -2.78 cycles; estimated location shift -2.60 cycles, 95% CI -2.82 to -2.37; P < 0.001) and preserved rank-ordering (Spearman rho = 0.84).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating that an instrument-free manual extraction format can exceed the efficiency of an automated reference workflow, enabling quality-assured influenza subtyping beyond centralised laboratories.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that SmartLid could decentralise influenza molecular testing, improving access to timely subtyping and supporting surveillance and clinical decision-making in resource-limited settings.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted at a single National Influenza Centre with a specific specimen set from one season, limiting generalisability; however, the strong statistical significance and consistency across subtypes and specimen types support moderate evidence strength.

title_zh: 快速磁珠核酸提取提升流感RT-qPCR灵敏度及分型成功率
source_body_en: Nucleic acid extraction remains the principal infrastructure barrier to molecular influenza testing outside centralised laboratories, since bead-based purification is normally tied to mains-powered extractors and trained operators. We evaluated SmartLid, a centrifugation-free format in which a removable magnetic key shuttles paramagnetic beads through pre-aliquoted lysis/binding, wash, and elution buffers without pipetting or powered instrumentation, against an automated magnetic-bead extractor (Nextractor NX-48S) on 311 nasopharyngeal specimens from the 2024-2025 influenza season at a National Influenza Centre. Paired eluates were amplified under identical monoplex RT-qPCR conditions for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3), and B/Victoria. Both methods gave 100% specificity (47/47 negatives; no false positives). Subtyping succeeded in 263/264 reference-positive specimens after SmartLid extraction versus 241/264 after automated extraction (99.62% versus 91.29%; difference 8.33 percentage points; discordant pairs 23 versus 1; McNemar P < 0.001). Across 240 complete pairs, cycle threshold (Ct) values were lower after SmartLid extraction (median paired difference -2.78 cycles; estimated location shift -2.60 cycles, 95% CI -2.82 to -2.37; P < 0.001) with rank-ordering of specimens conserved between methods (Spearman rho = 0.84). The advantage was preserved across all three subtypes and in both fresh and frozen specimens (adjusted P < 0.001). Specimens recovered only after SmartLid extraction had higher Ct values than dual-detected specimens (median 34.37 versus 28.54; P < 0.001), locating the gain near the assay detection limit. An instrument-free manual format can therefore exceed the extraction efficiency of an automated reference workflow, extending quality-assured influenza subtyping beyond centralised laboratories.
abstract_zh: 核酸提取仍是分子流感检测在非中心化实验室开展的主要基础设施瓶颈,因为磁珠纯化通常依赖于市电供电的提取仪和经过培训的操作人员。我们在2024–2025流感季期间,于一家国家流感中心对311份鼻咽拭子标本,评估了SmartLid(一种无离心格式,其中可移除的磁性钥匙可在预分装的裂解/结合、洗涤和洗脱缓冲液中转运顺磁珠,无需移液或电动设备)与自动磁珠提取仪(Nextractor NX-48S)的性能。将两种方法提取的洗脱液在相同单重RT-qPCR条件下扩增流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒及乙型Victoria系流感病毒。两种方法均实现100%特异性(47/47阴性;无假阳性)。SmartLid提取后,分型在264份参考阳性标本中成功263份,而自动提取后成功241份(99.62% vs 91.29%;差异8.33个百分点;不一致样本对23 vs 1;McNemar检验P < 0.001)。在240份完整配对样本中,SmartLid提取后的循环阈值(Ct)值更低(配对中位数差值-2.78个循环;估计位置偏移-2.60个循环,95%置信区间-2.82至-2.37;P < 0.001),且标本在两种方法间的排序保持一致(Spearman rho = 0.84)。该优势在三种亚型及新鲜与冰冻标本中均保持(校正P < 0.001)。仅在SmartLid提取后检测到的标本,其Ct值高于双检标本(中位数34.37 vs 28.54;P < 0.001),表明增益出现在检测限附近。因此,无仪器手动格式可超越自动参考工作流程的提取效率,使质量保证的流感分型扩展至非中心化实验室。

title: An outbreak report of Influenza A(H3) among residents of a large nursing home in northern Italy: attack rates, clinical features and outcomes
abstract: Abstract Background Nursing homes are high-risk settings for Influenza outbreaks, and the 2025–2026 Influenza season has been characterised by an earlier-than-usual epidemic onset globally with the emergence of a novel Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K strain including mutations that were not present in the strains of the 2025–2026 seasonal vaccine. Detailed outbreak investigations are essential to inform Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) strategies in these high-risk yet often neglected settings. Methods This is an outbreak report originating from data collected within an ongoing prospective surveillance in a 375-bed publicly funded nursing home in northern Italy. Surveillance for acute respiratory infection (ARI) was applied to all residents enrolled in the study (November-December 2025). Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from all ARI cases and analysed for Influenza A(H3). Cases were defined as residents with ARI and laboratory-confirmed Influenza A(H3). Attack rates (ARs), case-hospitalisation rate (CHR), and case-fatality rate (CFR) were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. Findings are here reported according to the Outbreak Reports and Intervention Studies of Nosocomial infection (ORION) guidelines. Results Of 217 involved residents (median age 88 years, 83% Influenza vaccinated), 50 (AR = 23%; 95% CI 17.6–29.2) had laboratory-confirmed Influenza A(H3). Fever (89.8%) and cough (81.6%) were the predominant symptoms. Median symptom duration was 3 days (range 1–14 days). The CHR was 8% (4/50; 95% CI 2.2–19.2) and the CFR was 0.0% (0/50; 95% CI 0.0-7.1) among confirmed cases. Conclusions This outbreak of Influenza A(H3) documented an overall attack rate slightly below the published median for nursing home outbreaks, with a low CHR and no confirmed deaths among laboratory-confirmed cases. The outbreak commenced in week 48, earlier than the historical Italian epidemic onset, underscoring the need for proactive surveillance, sustained attention to Influenza vaccination and IPC measures in long-term care facilities even ahead of the traditional winter peak.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 养老院是甲型流感暴发的高风险场所,2025–2026流感季在全球范围内呈现出较往年提前的流行起始特征,并出现了新型甲型流感病毒亚分支K株(包括未在2025–2026季节性流感株中检出的突变)。详细的流行病学调查对于指导这些高风险但常被忽视的场所的感染预防与控制(IPC)策略至关重要。方法 本研究为一项基于意大利北部一家375床位公立养老院持续前瞻性队列研究的病例报告。急性呼吸道感染(ARI)监测于2025年11月至12月在所有入组居民中实施。对所有ARI病例采集鼻咽拭子并检测甲型H3N2流感病毒。病例定义为出现ARI且实验室确诊为甲型H3N2流感病毒的居民。计算感染率(AR)、病例住院率(CHR)与病例死亡率(CFR),并提供95%置信区间。研究结果依据医院感染报告与干预研究ORION指南报告。结果 在217名参与居民中(中位年龄88岁,83%接种过流感疫苗),50例(感染率为23%;95%置信区间17.6–29.2)实验室确诊为甲型H3N2流感病毒。发热(89.8%)与咳嗽(81.6%)为主要症状。症状中位持续时间为3天(范围1–14天)。病例住院率为8%(4/50;95%置信区间2.2–19.2),病例死亡率为0.0%(0/50;95%置信区间0.0–7.1)。结论 本病例报告显示甲型H3N2流感病毒感染的整体感染率略低于养老院流感暴发的已发表中位数,病例住院率较低且实验室确诊病例中无确诊死亡。该暴发始于第48周,较意大利历史流行起始时间提前,凸显在传统冬季高峰前需采取主动监测、持续关注流感病毒变异株与加强长期护理机构感染预防控制措施的必要性。

title: Patterns and Predictors of Influenza Vaccination Uptake Among Healthcare Personnel in Kuwait: A Nationwide Multi-Season Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Healthcare personnel (HP) are a priority group for seasonal influenza vaccination due to their increased occupational exposure and potential to transmit influenza in healthcare settings. This study examined patterns and factors associated with in-season influenza vaccination uptake among HP in Kuwait. Methods: A nationwide observational study was conducted using Ministry of Health (MOH) administrative records covering the 2022/2023 through 2024/2025 influenza seasons. A person–season dataset was constructed, comprising one observation per HP for each of the three seasons. The primary outcome was in-season influenza vaccination, defined as receipt of an influenza vaccine between September and March of a given study season. Independent variables included age, sex, nationality, governorate of residence, profession, managerial position, previous-year influenza vaccination status, and pre-season sickness absence duration (days). Generalized estimating equations (GEE) logistic regression model with an exchangeable correlation structure was used to estimate factors associated with vaccination uptake. Results: The final analytic dataset included 48,886 HP contributing 146,658 person–season observations across three influenza seasons. Overall, in-season vaccination uptake was 8.7%, and repeated vaccination across seasons was uncommon. Older age, male sex, non-Kuwaiti nationality, and being a physician were independently associated with higher odds of in-season influenza vaccination. Previous-year influenza vaccination was the strongest predictor of current-season vaccination uptake (aOR 2.01, 95% CI 1.87–2.16; p < 0.001). Compared with HP with no pre-season sickness absence, those with 1–3 pre-season sickness absence days had slightly higher adjusted odds of vaccination (aOR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03–1.14), whereas those with ≥8 days had lower adjusted odds (aOR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.97). Conclusions: In-season influenza vaccination uptake among HP in Kuwait was low across three consecutive influenza seasons, with limited continuity of annual vaccination. Previous-year vaccination was the strongest predictor of current-season vaccination uptake, while the association between pre-season sickness absence and vaccination varied by absence duration. These findings support continued efforts to improve and sustain in-season influenza vaccination uptake among HP, while further research is needed to clarify the factors underlying vaccination decisions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Healthcare personnel (HP) face occupational exposure to seasonal influenza, yet vaccination uptake remains suboptimal, creating a risk for nosocomial transmission. The study addressed the knowledge gap on patterns and predictors of in-season influenza vaccination among HP in Kuwait to inform targeted interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide observational study was conducted using Ministry of Health administrative records spanning the 2022/2023 through 2024/2025 influenza seasons. A person–season dataset included 48,886 HP contributing 146,658 observations, with independent variables covering demographic, occupational, and health-related factors.
analysis.methods: In-season influenza vaccination was defined as receipt of an influenza vaccine between September and March of a given season. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) logistic regression with an exchangeable correlation structure estimated factors associated with vaccination uptake, adjusting for age, sex, nationality, governorate, profession, managerial position, previous-year vaccination status, and pre-season sickness absence duration.
analysis.main_results: Overall in-season vaccination uptake was 8.7%, with repeated vaccination across seasons being uncommon. Older age, male sex, non-Kuwaiti nationality, and being a physician were independently associated with higher odds of vaccination. Previous-year vaccination was the strongest predictor (aOR 2.01, 95% CI 1.87–2.16; p < 0.001). Pre-season sickness absence showed a non-linear association: 1–3 days slightly increased odds (aOR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03–1.14), while ≥8 days decreased odds (aOR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.97).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the low uptake and limited continuity as evidence of persistent barriers to vaccination among HP in Kuwait. They highlighted the dominant role of previous-year vaccination as a predictor, suggesting that interventions should prioritize sustaining annual uptake rather than initiating first-time vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings indicate that targeted strategies are needed to improve in-season influenza vaccination among HP in Kuwait, particularly focusing on groups with lower uptake such as younger staff and those with prolonged pre-season sickness absence. The study also underscores the importance of maintaining vaccination records to support continuity of care.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on administrative records, which may lack granular data on individual attitudes, beliefs, or access barriers. The observational design limits causal inference, and generalizability to other settings or populations remains uncertain. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide observational study examined in-season influenza vaccination uptake among 48,886 healthcare personnel (HP) in Kuwait across three consecutive seasons (2022/2023–2024/2025). title_zh: 科威特医护人员季节性流感疫苗接种接种模式及预测因素:一项全国多季节研究
source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Healthcare personnel (HP) are a priority group for seasonal influenza vaccination due to their increased occupational exposure and potential to transmit influenza in healthcare settings. This study examined patterns and factors associated with in-season influenza vaccination uptake among HP in Kuwait. Methods: A nationwide observational study was conducted using Ministry of Health (MOH) administrative records covering the 2022/2023 through 2024/2025 influenza seasons. A person–season dataset was constructed, comprising one observation per HP for each of the three seasons. The primary outcome was in-season influenza vaccination, defined as receipt of an influenza vaccine between September and March of a given study season. Independent variables included age, sex, nationality, governorate of residence, profession, managerial position, previous-year influenza vaccination status, and pre-season sickness absence duration (days). Generalized estimating equations (GEE) logistic regression model with an exchangeable correlation structure was used to estimate factors associated with vaccination uptake. Results: The final analytic dataset included 48,886 HP contributing 146,658 person–season observations across three influenza seasons. Overall, in-season vaccination uptake was 8.7%, and repeated vaccination across seasons was uncommon. Older age, male sex, non-Kuwaiti nationality, and being a physician were independently associated with higher odds of in-season influenza vaccination. Previous-year influenza vaccination was the strongest predictor of current-season vaccination uptake (aOR 2.01, 95% CI 1.87–2.16; p < 0.001). Compared with HP with no pre-season sickness absence, those with 1–3 pre-season sickness absence days had slightly higher adjusted odds of vaccination (aOR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03–1.14), whereas those with ≥8 days had lower adjusted odds (aOR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.97). Conclusions: In-season influenza vaccination uptake among HP in Kuwait was low across three consecutive influenza seasons, with limited continuity of annual vaccination. Previous-year vaccination was the strongest predictor of current-season vaccination uptake, while the association between pre-season sickness absence and vaccination varied by absence duration. These findings support continued efforts to improve and sustain in-season influenza vaccination uptake among HP, while further research is needed to clarify the factors underlying vaccination decisions.

title: Clinical and epidemiological profiles of six respiratory pathogens in hospitalized children in Lixin County, Anhui, China (2024–2025)
abstract: Background Acute respiratory infections are caused by a diverse range of pathogens. This study aimed to investigate the epidemiological profiles and clinical features of major respiratory pathogens by analyzing their detection rates in hospitalized pediatric patients. Methods Nasopharyngeal swab specimens were retrospectively enrolled from pediatric inpatients diagnosed with acute respiratory infections at the Department of Pediatrics, Lixin County People's Hospital, between February 2024 and August 2025. All specimens were subjected to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays targeting six major respiratory pathogens, namely adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A virus, influenza B virus, parainfluenza virus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae . Based on the PCR results, we further delineated the epidemiological trends, age-stratified distribution, and corresponding clinical profiles associated with each identified pathogen. Results The epidemiological and clinical profiles of the six detected respiratory pathogens are summarized below. In brief, the overall positivity rate of pathogens exhibited winter-spring predominance, with adenovirus and RSV showing the broadest outbreak windows (November–July and November–May, respectively), while influenza A was more restricted (December–March). Mycoplasma pneumoniae displayed a sporadic annual pattern without a statistically significant seasonal peak. Age distribution varied substantially: RSV targeted children 1 year, and influenza A showed a slight infant-toddler predominance. Clinically, while fever and cough were universal, RSV was distinguished by a significantly elevated wheezing rate (27.57% vs. 3.97%–9.52% for others), Febrile seizures were most frequently observed in influenza A virus infections (6.29%), followed by adenovirus (3.57%). Dyspnea or cyanosis was uniformly rare across all pathogens (≤ 0.45%). Conclusion During the winter season, multiple respiratory pathogens tend to circulate actively. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 急性呼吸道感染由多种病原体引起。本研究旨在通过分析住院儿童患者的病原体检出率,调查主要呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征与临床特点。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究回顾性纳入利辛县人民医院儿科诊断为急性呼吸道感染的住院患儿的鼻咽拭子标本,时间为2024年2月至2025年8月。研究对象为2024–2025年安徽省利辛县的住院儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 所有标本均采用聚合酶链反应(PCR)检测六种主要呼吸道病原体,包括腺病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、甲型流感病毒、乙型流感病毒、副流感病毒及肺炎支原体。基于PCR结果,进一步分析各病原体的流行病学趋势、年龄分层分布及对应临床特征。
elements_zh.main_results: 六种呼吸道病原体的流行病学与临床特征总结如下。总体阳性率呈冬春季节高发,其中腺病毒与呼吸道合胞病毒的流行窗口最长(分别为11月至次年7月、11月至次年5月),甲型流感病毒则相对局限(12月至次年3月)。肺炎支原体呈散发年度模式,无统计学意义的季节性高峰。年龄分布差异显著:呼吸道合胞病毒主要感染1岁儿童,甲型流感病毒则略偏向婴幼儿。临床上,发热与咳嗽为普遍症状,而呼吸道合胞病毒的喘息发生率显著升高(27.57%,其他病原体为3.97%–9.52%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 不同病原体引起的急性呼吸道感染在年龄分布与临床表现上存在差异。结合当地流行病学数据,这些特征有助于临床医师快速识别可能的病原体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可结合当地流行病学数据,帮助临床医生迅速识别可能的致病病原体。这些特征可以为 监测 和 诊断 儿童呼吸道感染策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告具体研究局限。证据基于PCR检测与回顾性数据,可能引入一定偏倚与解释上的局限性。

title: Subtype-specific risk estimates of influenza under extreme weather events in a subtropical coastal city: high humidity as a major factor associated with forecasting implications
abstract: Meteorological conditions are important environmental determinants of influenza transmission; however, the health impacts of extreme weather events (EWEs) remain insufficiently characterized, particularly in subtropical coastal regions. Using Xiamen, China, as a case study, we systematically evaluated the heterogeneous associations between EWEs on influenza and quantified their independent predictive contributions. Daily surveillance data (2013–2024) were analyzed using distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNM) to assess risks of 11 EWE categories across influenza subtypes and population strata, adjusting for air pollutants and population mobility. Random forest (RF) modeling further evaluated predictive contributions. Pronounced EWE-specific effects emerged: extreme high humidity event (EHRHUE) most strongly associated with influenza B(Yamagata) (21-day cumulative relative risk [CRR] = 2.51), while extreme low temperature event (ELTEME) most strongly associated with A(H3N2) (21-day CRR = 1.72). Extreme low wind speed event (ELWINE) and extreme long sunshine duration event (EHSSDE) showed elevated risks for B(Yamagata) (21-day CRR = 3.11) and A(H3N2) (21-day CRR = 3.36), respectively. Feature importance identified EHRHUE as the dominant predictor (35.59% contribution), followed by PM10 (18.64%). Incorporating EWEs into RF improved performance: Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) increased 26.82%; other metrics also enhanced. This study confirms that EWEs were significantly and heterogeneously associated with influenza transmission in subtropical coastal cities, with EHRHUE, PM10, and temperature as key environmental predictors. Integrating EWEs into predictive models enhances influenza forecasting accuracy and provides a scientific foundation for climate-adaptive early warning systems and precision public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between extreme weather events (EWEs) and influenza transmission in a subtropical coastal city, Xiamen, China. The research highlights the need to understand how environmental factors influence influenza spread, particularly in regions where such impacts are not well characterized. Using daily surveillance data from 2013 to 2024, the study applied distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNM) and random forest (RF) analysis to assess the risks of 11 EWE categories across influenza subtypes, adjusting for air pollutants and population mobility. The main results showed that extreme high humidity events were most strongly linked to influenza B(Yamagata), while extreme low temperature events were most associated with A(H3N2). The study also found that incorporating EWEs into predictive models improved forecasting accuracy. The authors interpret these findings as significant and heterogeneous associations between EWEs and influenza transmission, identifying EHRHUE, PM10, and temperature as key environmental predictors. These results have important implications for developing climate-adaptive early warning systems and precision public health interventions. However, the study's findings are based on abstract-only evidence, and the analysis is limited to the specific environmental factors and subtypes mentioned.

title_zh: 亚型特异性流感在极端天气事件下的风险估计:以高湿度为主要预测因子在亚热带沿海城市的预测意义
source_body_en: Meteorological conditions are important environmental determinants of influenza transmission; however, the health impacts of extreme weather events (EWEs) remain insufficiently characterized, particularly in subtropical coastal regions. Using Xiamen, China, as a case study, we systematically evaluated the heterogeneous associations between EWEs on influenza and quantified their independent predictive contributions. Daily surveillance data (2013–2024) were analyzed using distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNM) to assess risks of 11 EWE categories across influenza subtypes and population strata, adjusting for air pollutants and population mobility. Random forest (RF) modeling further evaluated predictive contributions. Pronounced EWE-specific effects emerged: extreme high humidity event (EHRHUE) most strongly associated with influenza B(Yamagata) (21-day cumulative relative risk [CRR] = 2.51), while extreme low temperature event (ELTEME) most strongly associated with A(H3N2) (21-day CRR = 1.72). Extreme low wind speed event (ELWINE) and extreme long sunshine duration event (EHSSDE) showed elevated risks for B(Yamagata) (21-day CRR = 3.11) and A(H3N2) (21-day CRR = 3.36), respectively. Feature importance identified EHRHUE as the dominant predictor (35.59% contribution), followed by PM10 (18.64%). Incorporating EWEs into RF improved performance: Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) increased 26.82%; other metrics also enhanced. This study confirms that EWEs were significantly and heterogeneously associated with influenza transmission in subtropical coastal cities, with EHRHUE, PM10, and temperature as key environmental predictors. Integrating EWEs into predictive models enhances influenza forecasting accuracy and provides a scientific foundation for climate-adaptive early warning systems and precision public health interventions.
abstract_zh: 气象条件是流感传播的重要环境决定因素;然而,极端天气事件(EWEs)对健康的影响仍未得到充分表征,尤其是在亚热带沿海地区。本研究以中国厦门为案例,系统评估了EWEs对流感的异质性关联,并量化其独立预测贡献。采用分布滞后非线性模型(DLNM)分析2013–2024年每日监测数据,评估11类EWEs对不同流感亚型和人群分层的风险,并调整了空气污染物和人口流动性。随机森林(RF)模型进一步评估了预测贡献。显著的EWEs特异性效应显现:极端高湿度事件(EHRHUE)与流感B(Yamagata)亚型关联最强(21天累积相对风险[CRR] = 2.51),而极端低温事件(ELTEME)与甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09关联最强(21天CRR = 1.72)。极端低风速事件(ELWINE)和极端长日照时长事件(EHSSDE)分别对B(Yamagata)亚型(21天CRR = 3.11)和甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09(21天CRR = 3.36)显示出较高风险。特征重要性分析显示EHRHUE为主导预测因子(贡献度35.59%),其次为PM10(18.64%)。将EWEs纳入RF模型后,性能提升:Nash–Sutcliffe效率(NSE)提高26.82%,其他指标亦有改善。本研究证实EWEs与亚热带沿海城市流感传播显著且异质性关联,其中EHRHUE、PM10和温度为关键环境预测因子。将EWEs纳入预测模型可提升流感预测准确性,并为气候适应性早期预警系统和精准公共卫生干预提供科学依据。

title: Beyond Entry: Evaluating the Internal Spread Risk of highly pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1 in Australia
abstract: Abstract The highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N1 is currently spreading worldwide, with Oceania remaining the only continent largely unaffected until recently, when positive cases in migratory birds were detected in Western Australia and South Australia, and, more recently, a suspected case in New South Wales. Furthermore, H5N1 in Heard Island has caused widespread mortality in elephant seal pups. Migratory waterfowl and shorebirds, recognised as key vectors of avian influenza viruses (AIV), connect Australia with global transmission networks. Here, we developed an agent-based model to predict the spread of H5N1 following potential incursions across different regions of Australia. Our results suggest that the incursion region strongly affects outbreak spread and duration. The spread of H5N1 in Australia creates a substantial risk for poultry outbreaks and potential spillover into wildlife populations, particularly in ecologically sensitive breeding areas. These findings provide critical insights for informing national preparedness, guiding targeted surveillance, and strengthening One Health strategies to mitigate the impact of HPAI in Australia.
authors: Catarina do Carmo Norte dos Santos

Here, we developed an agent-based model to predict the spread of H5N1 following potential incursions across different regions of Australia. Our results suggest that the incursion region strongly affects outbreak spread and duration. The spread of H5N1 in Australia creates a substantial risk for poultry outbreaks and potential spillover into wildlife populations, particularly in ecologically sensitive breeding areas. These findings provide critical insights for informing national preparedness, guiding targeted surveillance, and strengthening One Health strategies to mitigate the impact of HPAI in Australia.

title: Systemic removal of host restriction factors enables rapid, scalable virus production for cell culture-based vaccine development
abstract: The efficiency of cell culture-based vaccine production is fundamentally constrained by the antiviral defenses of host cells, creating a major bottleneck for rapid and large-scale vaccine manufacturing. Key antiviral proteins-such as RNase L, PKR, and JAK1 act as intrinsic brakes on viral replication, limiting efficient propagation of many clinically relevant viruses. To overcome this challenge, we generated HEK293T, Vero, and MDCK cell lines with targeted knockouts of multiple antiviral genes. Notably, these engineered cells maintained normal growth and viability while supporting markedly increased viral yields. Multi-gene deletions enhance the replication of both enveloped viruses, including influenza A virus, pseudotyped lentivirus, and porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV), and non-enveloped viruses such as coxsackievirus. The magnitude of enhancement scaled proportionally with the number of genes disrupted. By systematically removing host restriction factors, this platform provides a versatile and powerful strategy for accelerating viral propagation, offering a strong foundation for more efficient development and large-scale production of cell culture-based anti-viral vaccines.

title: Systems-level insights into age-dependent innate immune responses in influenza B infection
abstract: Aging is known to alter innate immune function, increasing susceptibility to viral infections, yet its specific effects on influenza B virus (IBV) infection remain poorly characterized. To address this gap, we developed a preclinical mouse model using a clinically relevant IBV strain Inf B/Phuket/3073/2013 to compare innate immune responses between young adult and aged mice, with a particular focus on age-related transcriptional and proteomic alterations in lung during infection. Bulk RNA sequencing and proteomics analysis of lung tissue harvested post-infection revealed distinct age-dependent transcriptional profiles. Bulk RNA-seq analysis identified 1,350 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), of which 824 exhibited an aged-biased expression pattern and were significantly upregulated in the lungs of influenza B virus-infected aged mice. Functional enrichment of these DEGs indicated perturbations in innate immune signaling, apoptosis, and pathways related to cellular stress and DNA damage in aged mice. There are several differentially expressed proteins that have been identified in young adult and aged influenza B infection. Among these differentially expressed proteins, some commonly co-expressed proteins have a role in virus entry, signaling pathways, and interferon response. Real-time PCR analysis confirmed altered expression of key innate immune genes, including Toll-like receptors (TLRs), interferon regulatory factors (IRF7 and IRF9), key antiviral genes (IFIT -2, IFIT-3 and STAT-1) and type I and II interferons (IFN-α, IFN-β, IFN-γ). Notably, young adult mice exhibited a more coordinated and robust activation of antiviral pathways, whereas aged mice demonstrated delayed and aberrant immune responses, characterized by excessive inflammation and impaired interferon signaling. IMPORTANCE: This study provides a comprehensive system-level analysis of age-driven alterations in innate immunity during influenza B virus (IBV) infection. While prior evidence has established that aging impairs antiviral responses across various viral infections, our findings specifically demonstrate that IBV infection in aged mice leads to a disproportionate and dysregulated transcriptional activation of innate immune pathways, including excessive type I interferon signaling and altered inflammatory mediator profiles, and uncover the potential therapeutic targets to improve health outcomes in the elderly population on influenza infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Aging is known to alter innate immune function and increase susceptibility to viral infections, yet the specific effects of aging on influenza B virus (IBV) infection remain poorly characterized, creating a knowledge gap that this study aimed to address.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a preclinical mouse model with a clinically relevant IBV strain (Inf B/Phuket/3073/2013) to compare innate immune responses between young adult and aged mice, focusing on age-related transcriptional and proteomic alterations in lung tissue during infection.
analysis.methods: Bulk RNA sequencing and proteomics were performed on lung tissue harvested post-infection to identify differentially expressed genes and proteins, and real-time PCR was used to confirm altered expression of key innate immune genes including TLRs, IRF7, IRF9, IFIT-2, IFIT-3, STAT-1, and interferons.
analysis.main_results: Bulk RNA-seq identified 1,350 differentially expressed genes, with 824 showing aged-biased upregulation in infected lungs, and functional enrichment indicated perturbations in innate immune signaling, apoptosis, and stress-related pathways in aged mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating that IBV infection in aged mice leads to disproportionate and dysregulated transcriptional activation of innate immune pathways, including excessive type I interferon signaling and altered inflammatory mediator profiles, highlighting potential therapeutic targets for improving health outcomes in the elderly.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that age-dependent innate immune dysregulation during IBV infection may inform targeted interventions to enhance antiviral responses and reduce excessive inflammation in elderly populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its preclinical mouse model design, which may not fully recapitulate human immune responses, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of human validation and potential confounding from model-specific immune dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated age-dependent innate immune responses during influenza B virus (IBV) infection using a preclinical mouse model with the clinically relevant IBV strain Inf B/Phuket/3073/2013. Bulk RNA sequencing and proteomics of lung tissue revealed 1,350 differentially expressed genes, with 824 showing aged-biased upregulation and functional enrichment in innate immune signaling, apoptosis, and stress-related pathways. Real-time PCR confirmed altered expression of key antiviral genes including TLRs, IRF7, IRF9, IFIT-2, IFIT-3, STAT-1, and interferons. Young adult mice exhibited coordinated antiviral pathway activation, whereas aged mice showed delayed and aberrant responses characterized by excessive inflammation and impaired interferon signaling. The authors interpret these findings as evidence of disproportionate and dysregulated innate immune activation in aged hosts, suggesting potential therapeutic targets to improve outcomes in elderly populations. While the study provides system-level insights, its preclinical nature and lack of human validation limit generalizability, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

title: A CRISPR-based ‘dam-break drainage’ sensing architecture for rapid, affordable and ultrasensitive pathogen detection
abstract: Abstract Nucleic acid testing is important for infectious-disease diagnosis, but combining high sensitivity with accessible testing remains challenging. Here we show a chip-based visual detection strategy for one or two viral RNA targets that involves only sample loading, without further instrumentation or manual actuation. Target-activated CRISPR-Cas13a alters the wettability of a molecular barrier, causing liquid to cross a preset threshold and generate a dam-break drainage signal. The chip detects a single target at 10 aM within 2 min and two targets at 100 aM within 5 min, with costs of $0.20 and $0.30 per test, respectively. We further establish a practical clinical-sample workflow combining room-temperature lysis with RNase inhibition and validate the platform across 40 nasal-swab samples tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus and influenza B virus, with results concordant with RT–PCR. This threshold-based fluidic strategy provides a route towards rapid, low-cost and instrument-free molecular testing outside centralized laboratories.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a CRISPR-based 'dam-break drainage' sensing architecture for rapid, affordable and ultrasensitive pathogen detection. The research aimed to address the challenge of combining high sensitivity with accessible testing for infectious diseases. The chip-based strategy enables visual detection of one or two viral RNA targets without additional instrumentation, and the method involves room-temperature lysis and RNase inhibition. The platform was validated using 40 nasal-swab samples for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus, and influenza B virus, showing concordance with RT–PCR results. The chip can detect a single target at 10 aM within 2 minutes and two targets at 100 aM within 5 minutes, with costs of $0.20 and $0.30 per test, respectively. The authors interpret this as a novel approach for rapid, low-cost, and instrument-free molecular testing outside centralized laboratories. The findings have potential significance for improving surveillance and diagnosis of seasonal influenza viruses in resource-limited settings. title_zh: 基于CRISPR的‘决堤排水’传感架构:实现快速、经济且超灵敏的病原体检测
source_body_en: Abstract Nucleic acid testing is important for infectious-disease diagnosis, but combining high sensitivity with accessible testing remains challenging. Here we show a chip-based visual detection strategy for one or two viral RNA targets that involves only sample loading, without further instrumentation or manual actuation. Target-activated CRISPR-Cas13a alters the wettability of a molecular barrier, causing liquid to cross a preset threshold and generate a dam-break drainage signal. The chip detects a single target at 10 aM within 2 min and two targets at 100 aM within 5 min, with costs of $0.20 and $0.30 per test, respectively. We further establish a practical clinical-sample workflow combining room-temperature lysis with RNase inhibition and validate the platform across 40 nasal-swab samples tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus and influenza B virus, with results concordant with RT–PCR. This threshold-based fluidic strategy provides a route towards rapid, low-cost and instrument-free molecular testing outside centralized laboratories.

title: A bispecific antibody targeting conserved hemagglutinin epitopes confers broad protection against H7 avian influenza and accelerates viral clearance via localized respiratory delivery
abstract: The continuous antigenic drift of zoonotic H7 avian influenza viruses remains a significant global public health threat. While monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting the hemagglutinin (HA) head offer potent neutralization, their efficacy is often undermined by rapid viral escape. In this study, we systematically mapped the antigenic architecture of the H7 HA head domain using a panel of 30 murine mAbs. By integrating epitope mapping with longitudinal evolutionary analysis of over 2,500 isolates, we identified highly conserved, functionally constrained residues, specifically G70, G132, N167, and M173, that remained nearly invariant over decades. Leveraging these insights, we engineered a chimeric bispecific antibody (BsAb-H7) to simultaneously engage two distinct, non-overlapping conserved epitopes. BsAb-H7 demonstrated broad neutralization breadth across divergent H7N9, H7N7, and H7N3 subtypes in vitro and exhibited a superior in vivo pharmacokinetic profile. In lethal murine challenge models, BsAb-H7 provided robust prophylactic and therapeutic protection against heterologous H7N7 infection. Notably, localized intranasal administration significantly outperformed systemic delivery by accelerating viral clearance and resolving pulmonary immunopathology during delayed intervention windows. These results demonstrate that bispecific targeting of conserved HA epitopes effectively enhances antiviral breadth and limits immune escape, providing a promising strategy for the development of broadly protective therapeutics against rapidly evolving H7 influenza viruses.

title: MoActiPred: an AI-Based bioactivity prediction model applied to the development of influenza neuraminidase inhibitors
abstract: Accurate prediction of small-molecule bioactivity is critical for accelerating drug discovery. Here, we report MoActiPred, a multimodal AI framework that integrates 2D molecular graphs, physicochemical descriptors, and 3D E (3)-equivariant geometric representations. Using a curated ChEMBL-derived influenza virus neuraminidase (NA) inhibitor dataset (1245 compounds; IC 50 threshold 20 nM), MoActiPred showed the strongest overall performance among the evaluated methods, including traditional machine-learning models (Random Forest, SVM, and XGBoost), SMILES-based language models (ChemBERTa, ChemFM, and PolyBERT), and graph-based baselines (MolCLR and SEGNN). On the public test set, MoActiPred obtained an accuracy of 0.952, MCC of 0.797, and F1 score of 0.898, while retaining high average precision, supporting the value of combining 2D and 3D representations. To evaluate its practical utility, MoActiPred was applied prospectively to 26 oseltamivir analogues designed, experimentally synthesised and evaluated against influenza A (H3N2) NA. The model correctly predicted 6 of 7 high-activity compounds (IC 50 100 μM). Docking, MD simulations, and water-map analyses indicated that the oseltamivir core of 5b occupies the conserved active site while its N -substituent engages the 150- and 430-cavities, with solvation-driven binding particularly favouring N2. These results support that MoActiPred’s utility in drug discovery research and identify 5b as a promising lead for further optimisation against influenza A (H3N2). Scientific contribution MoActiPred advances bioactivity prediction by integrating 2D molecular graphs, physicochemical descriptors, and 3D E (3)-equivariant geometric representations within a single multimodal framework. Compared with conventional machine-learning models, SMILES-based language models, and graph-based baselines, MoActiPred achieved stronger classification performance on the curated and public neuraminidase inhibitor datasets, demonstrating the value of combined 2D/3D molecular representation learning. Its prospective utility was further supported by in-house synthesis of a focused oseltamivir-analogue series followed by enzymatic and cell-based biological activity testing.

title: Negotiating security and resilience: planning conundrums for avian influenza control in Great Britain’s poultry systems
abstract: Abstract The outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza in Great Britain between 2021 and 2026 represent the most severe period of virus activity recorded in the country, prompting renewed scrutiny of how biosecurity is conceptualised and practised within poultry systems. This paper examines how the structure of poultry sectors, producing meat, eggs, and game birds, shape disease risk and the possibilities for a resilient poultry ecology. Using a production and distribution network approach, we combine a desk-based review of industry, policy, grey, and published literature with qualitative data from 19 in-depth interviews, supplemented by field visits and engagement in stakeholder events. Our analysis shows that highly integrated and geographically concentrated poultry meat and layer systems interact with wild and semi-wild birds in ways which generate distinct challenges. Concentration of production and processing infrastructure, aging housing stock, consumer demand for free-range, and large-scale releases of game birds impact decisions around poultry governance and questions of risk around avian influenza incursion. We identify two cross-cutting ‘entanglements’ that condition avian influenza virus vulnerability: (1) poultry planning, where fragmented and often contested land-use decisions interact with environmental and biodiversity policies to shape exposure to wild and semi-wild ecologies; and (2) the insuring of poultry, where a market failure in private avian influenza insurance and uneven and contested state compensation regimes differentially distribute risk across producers and sectors. We argue that farm-level biosecurity, while necessary, is insufficient to secure Britain’s poultry production under near-endemic avian influenza virus pressure. A more bio-resilient poultry future will require macro-level, multi-sectoral coordination that integrates spatial planning, infrastructure renewal, and equitable risk-sharing mechanisms for disease preparedness.

title: Air sampling in team congregate spaces for early detection of respiratory virus threats at the 2026 FIFA World CupTM
abstract: Objective.Respiratory infections are the leading cause of illness at major sporting events, yet surveillance relies on athletes recognising and reporting symptoms. We evaluated whether continuous air sampling with point-of-care molecular testing could detect respiratory-virus nucleic acids in an elite teams congregate spaces during competition, and whether the resulting signals were operationally useful. Methods.We performed a prospective, descriptive environmental-surveillance study following the Canadian mens national soccer team across five host cities during the 2026 FIFA World Cup (3 June to 4 July 2026). InBio Apollo bioaerosol samplers ran continuously in up to four teamdesignated rooms per hotel (physiotherapy, meal, equipment, and coaches room or hallway). Filters were changed approximately twice daily, eluted on-site, and tested with the Cepheid Xpert(R) Xpress SARS-CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus assay. A sample was considered positive if any cycle-threshold (Ct) value was reported, as less than 45, for a target. Results.Of 174 air filters, there were 13 detections of virus genetic material (9 SARS-CoV-2, 3 influenza A virus, 1 influenza B virus, 0 RSV). Detections were sparse early and clustered late in the tournament. An influenza A signal appeared the morning a player was sent home febrile, and SARS-CoV-2 signals coincided with visibly ill hotel staff, with signals falling after ill staff were excluded. Conclusion.Air sampling with point-of-care testing is feasible in the mobile environment of an elite team and can surface behavior-independent viral signals during competition that may offer opportunities for earlier precautionary actions. Summary BoxO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSRespiratory infections are the leading cause of illnesses at major sporting events, and conventional surveillance depends on athletes recognising and reporting symptoms, which misses presymptomatic, mild, and asymptomatic infections. Air sampling can detect respiratory viruses in congregate settings but has not been evaluated in elite team housing during competition. What this study addsContinuous air sampling with same-day point-of-care testing was feasible across a five-city World Cup campaign and detected SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and influenza B in shared team spaces even during the low-circulation Northern-hemisphere summer, with several signals coinciding with a febrile player and with visibly ill staff. How this study might affect research, practice or policyAir sampling offers a candidate behavior-independent method to generate an early-warning signal that could allow teams to escalate precautions selectively, minimizing virus exposures among athletes and team staff. Continuous bioaerosol sampling was performed in up to four team congregate spaces per hotel, typically the meal, equipment, physiotherapy, and coaches rooms, across five host cities during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Each samplers filter was eluted on-site and tested on a Cepheid GeneXpert SARS-CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus cartridge, giving a same-day, point-of-care result (top). Viral genetic material was detected in team-hotel air in every one of the five cities. The timeline shows sampling coverage as a horizontal band and each viral detection as a vertical tick on a single continuous time axis across the tournament, with detections sparse early and clustered in the final cities (middle). A positive air signal can trigger low-cost, low-regret responses before an outbreak is clinically apparent, such as masking, portable air purifiers, distancing and reduced occupancy, far-UVC lighting, reinforced ventilation, and excluding visibly ill personnel (bottom).

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the feasibility of using continuous air sampling with point-of-care molecular testing to detect respiratory viruses in congregate spaces of an elite sports team during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The research aimed to address the limitations of conventional surveillance methods that rely on athlete self-reporting, which can miss presymptomatic and asymptomatic infections. The study found that viral genetic material was detected in team-hotel air in all five host cities, with 13 positive detections out of 174 filters. These included 9 SARS-CoV-2, 3 influenza A virus, and 1 influenza B virus. Detections were sparse early in the tournament and clustered later, with some signals coinciding with a febrile player and with visibly ill hotel staff. The findings suggest that air sampling could provide an early-warning system for respiratory virus threats, enabling teams to take precautionary measures before outbreaks are clinically apparent. The study's results highlight the potential of this method for improving surveillance in high-risk environments, though the evidence is limited to the abstract and does not include detailed limitations or statistical analyses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道感染是大型体育赛事中最主要的疾病原因,但监测依赖运动员识别并报告症状。本研究旨在评估连续空气采样结合现场分子检测是否能在精英团队的集中活动空间内于比赛期间检测到呼吸道病毒核酸,以及由此产生的信号是否具有操作实用性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们开展了一项前瞻性描述性环境-监测研究,在2026年国际足联世界杯期间(2026年6月3日至7月4日)对加拿大国家男子足球队在五个宿主城市的活动进行了追踪。InBio Apollo生物气溶胶采样器在每家酒店的最多四间球队指定房间内连续运行,包括理疗室、餐厅、器材室以及教练室或走廊。
elements_zh.methods: 滤器每天大约更换两次,在现场进行洗脱,并使用Cepheid Xpert® Xpress SARS-CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus试剂盒进行检测。若任一靶标的循环阈值(Ct)值报告为小于45,则样本判定为阳性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在174个空气过滤器中,检测到13例病毒遗传物质(9例SARS-CoV-2、3例甲型流感病毒、1例乙型流感病毒、0例呼吸道合胞病毒)。检测结果在锦标赛早期稀疏,晚期集中。一名球员因发热被送回家当天早晨出现甲型流感病毒信号,而SARS-CoV-2信号与酒店可视患病员工同时出现,在排除患病员工后信号消退。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在精英团队的移动环境中,通过即时检测进行空气采样是可行的,并能在比赛期间发现与行为无关的病毒信号,这可能为更早采取预防措施提供机会。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 空气采样提供了一种候选的行为无关方法,可生成早期预警信号,使团队能够有选择地加强防护措施,从而最大限度地减少运动员及团队工作人员的病毒暴露风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告该研究的局限性或证据强度。

title_zh: 2026年国际足联世界杯TM期间在团队集合场所进行空气采样以早期检测呼吸道病毒威胁
source_body_en: Objective.Respiratory infections are the leading cause of illness at major sporting events, yet surveillance relies on athletes recognising and reporting symptoms. We evaluated whether continuous air sampling with point-of-care molecular testing could detect respiratory-virus nucleic acids in an elite teams congregate spaces during competition, and whether the resulting signals were operationally useful. Methods.We performed a prospective, descriptive environmental-surveillance study following the Canadian mens national soccer team across five host cities during the 2026 FIFA World Cup (3 June to 4 July 2026). InBio Apollo bioaerosol samplers ran continuously in up to four teamdesignated rooms per hotel (physiotherapy, meal, equipment, and coaches room or hallway). Filters were changed approximately twice daily, eluted on-site, and tested with the Cepheid Xpert(R) Xpress SARS-CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus assay. A sample was considered positive if any cycle-threshold (Ct) value was reported, as less than 45, for a target. Results.Of 174 air filters, there were 13 detections of virus genetic material (9 SARS-CoV-2, 3 influenza A virus, 1 influenza B virus, 0 RSV). Detections were sparse early and clustered late in the tournament. An influenza A signal appeared the morning a player was sent home febrile, and SARS-CoV-2 signals coincided with visibly ill hotel staff, with signals falling after ill staff were excluded. Conclusion.Air sampling with point-of-care testing is feasible in the mobile environment of an elite team and can surface behavior-independent viral signals during competition that may offer opportunities for earlier precautionary actions. Summary BoxO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSRespiratory infections are the leading cause of illnesses at major sporting events, and conventional surveillance depends on athletes recognising and reporting symptoms, which misses presymptomatic, mild, and asymptomatic infections. Air sampling can detect respiratory viruses in congregate settings but has not been evaluated in elite team housing during competition. What this study addsContinuous air sampling with same-day point-of-care testing was feasible across a five-city World Cup campaign and detected SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and influenza B in shared team spaces even during the low-circulation Northern-hemisphere summer, with several signals coinciding with a febrile player and with visibly ill staff. How this study might affect research, practice or policyAir sampling offers a candidate behavior-independent method to generate an early-warning signal that could allow teams to escalate precautions selectively, minimizing virus exposures among athletes and team staff. Continuous bioaerosol sampling was performed in up to four team congregate spaces per hotel, typically the meal, equipment, physiotherapy, and coaches rooms, across five host cities during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Each samplers filter was eluted on-site and tested on a Cepheid GeneXpert SARS-CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus cartridge, giving a same-day, point-of-care result (top). Viral genetic material was detected in team-hotel air in every one of the five cities. The timeline shows sampling coverage as a horizontal band and each viral detection as a vertical tick on a single continuous time axis across the tournament, with detections sparse early and clustered in the final cities (middle). A positive air signal can trigger low-cost, low-regret responses before an outbreak is clinically apparent, such as masking, portable air purifiers, distancing and reduced occupancy, far-UVC lighting, reinforced ventilation, and excluding visibly ill personnel (bottom).
abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染是大型体育赛事中疾病的主要原因,但监测依赖运动员识别和报告症状。我们评估了连续空气采样与即时分子检测是否能在精英团队集中空间的比赛期间检测到呼吸道病毒核酸,以及由此产生的信号是否具有操作价值。方法。我们对加拿大男子国家足球队在2026年国际足联世界杯期间(2026年6月3日至7月4日)横跨五个宿主城市进行前瞻性描述性环境-监测研究。InBio Apollo生物气溶胶采样器持续在每家酒店最多四个团队指定房间(理疗室、餐厅、设备室和教练室或走廊)内运行。滤膜每天更换约两次,现场洗脱并使用Cepheid Xpert® Xpress SARS-CoV-2/流感/RSV plus试剂盒检测。若任何靶标的循环阈值(Ct)值小于45,则样本判定为阳性。结果。在174个空气滤膜中,检测到13次病毒遗传物质(9次SARS-CoV-2,3次甲型流感病毒,1次乙型流感病毒,0次RSV)。检测在赛事早期稀少,晚期集中。流感A信号出现在一名发热球员被送回家的当天早晨,而SARS-CoV-2信号与酒店工作人员出现明显症状同时出现,在患病工作人员被排除后信号消失。结论。在精英团队的移动环境中,空气采样与即时检测可行,可在比赛期间提供不依赖行为的病毒信号,可能为更早采取预防措施提供机会。摘要框已知内容本话题已知内容呼吸道感染是大型体育赛事中疾病的主要原因,传统监测依赖运动员识别和报告症状,但会错过症状前期、轻症和无症状感染。空气采样可在集中场所检测呼吸道病毒,但未在比赛期间的精英团队住宿环境中评估。本研究的新增内容在为期五城市世界杯赛事期间,连续空气采样与当日即时检测可行,即使在北半球夏季低流行期,也能在团队共享空间中检测到SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感和乙型流感,部分信号与发热球员及明显症状工作人员同时出现。本研究可能对研究、实践或政策的影响空气采样提供了一种不依赖行为的早期预警方法,可让团队选择性升级预防措施,最大限度减少运动员和团队工作人员的病毒暴露。中心图表O_FIG O_LINKSMALLFIG WIDTH=200 HEIGHT=157 SRC="FIGDIR/small/26360542v1_ufig1.gif" ALT="图1"> 查看大图(44K):org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@1bc3ae7org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@bf47dforg.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@7965forg.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@214a7a_HPS_FORMAT_FIGEXP M_FIG 比赛期间精英团队呼吸道病毒威胁的空气采样早期检测。在2026年国际足联世界杯期间,于五个宿主城市的酒店内最多四个团队集中空间(餐厅、设备室、理疗室和教练室或走廊)持续进行生物气溶胶采样。每个采样器的滤膜在现场洗脱,并使用Cepheid GeneXpert SARS-CoV-2/流感/RSV plus试剂盒进行当日即时检测(上图)。在五个城市的团队酒店空气中均检测到病毒遗传物质。时间线以横向条带表示采样覆盖范围,以垂直标记表示整个赛事单一连续时间轴上的每次病毒检测,检测在早期稀少而在后期城市集中(中图)。阳性空气信号可在暴发临床表现前触发低成本、低风险响应措施,如佩戴口罩、便携式空气净化器、保持距离与减少入住率、远-UVC照明、加强通风及排除明显症状人员(下图)。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道感染是大型体育赛事中最主要的疾病原因,但监测依赖运动员识别并报告症状。本研究旨在评估连续空气采样结合现场分子检测是否能在精英团队的集中活动空间内于比赛期间检测到呼吸道病毒核酸,以及由此产生的信号是否具有操作实用性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们开展了一项前瞻性描述性环境-监测研究,在2026年国际足联世界杯期间(2026年6月3日至7月4日)对加拿大国家男子足球队在五个宿主城市的活动进行了追踪。InBio Apollo生物气溶胶采样器在每家酒店的最多四间球队指定房间内连续运行,包括理疗室、餐厅、器材室以及教练室或走廊。
analysis_zh.methods: 滤器每天大约更换两次,在现场进行洗脱,并使用Cepheid Xpert® Xpress SARS-CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus试剂盒进行检测。若任一靶标的循环阈值(Ct)值报告为小于45,则样本判定为阳性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在174个空气过滤器中,检测到13例病毒遗传物质(9例SARS-CoV-2、3例甲型流感病毒、1例乙型流感病毒、0例呼吸道合胞病毒)。检测结果在锦标赛早期稀疏,晚期集中。一名球员因发热被送回家当天早晨出现甲型流感病毒信号,而SARS-CoV-2信号与酒店可视患病员工同时出现,在排除患病员工后信号消退。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在精英团队的移动环境中,通过即时检测进行空气采样是可行的,并能在比赛期间发现与行为无关的病毒信号,这可能为更早采取预防措施提供机会。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 空气采样提供了一种候选的行为无关方法,可生成早期预警信号,使团队能够有选择地加强防护措施,从而最大限度地减少运动员及团队工作人员的病毒暴露风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告该研究的局限性或证据强度。

title: Genç Hastada İnfluenza ile İlişkili ARDS Yönetimi: Tanıdan Tedaviye Multidisipliner Yaklaşım
abstract: İnfluenza enfeksiyonu çoğunlukla kendini sınırlayan üst solunum yolu enfeksiyonu şeklinde seyretmekle birlikte, nadiren ağır viral pnömoniye ve akut respiratuvar distres sendromuna (ARDS) yol açabilmektedir. Bu olgu sunumunda, altta yatan komorbiditesi bulunmayan 20 yaşındaki erkek hastada influenza A enfeksiyonuna sekonder, saatler içerisinde gelişen ağır ARDS tablosu ve yoğun bakım yönetimi sunulmuştur. Üst solunum yolu enfeksiyonu semptomları ile ilk başvurusunda belirgin patoloji saptanmayan hasta, yaklaşık 12 saat sonra ciddi dispne ve hipoksemi ile tekrar başvurmuş, acilde çekilen toraks BT’de bilateral yaygın buzlu cam ve konsolidasyon alanları izlenmiştir. Viral pnömoniye sekonder gelişen ağır ARDS nedeniyle hasta elektif olarak entübe edilerek yoğun bakım ünitesine alınmış ve akciğer koruyucu mekanik ventilasyon stratejileri uygulanmıştır. Solunum yolu örneklerinden yapılan polimeraz zincir reaksiyonu (PCR) testinde İnfluenza A(H3N2) saptanmıştır. Yoğun bakım izlemi sırasında oksijenizasyonu ve radyolojik bulguları hızla düzelen hasta yatışının beşinci gününde ekstübe edilmiş ve yedinci gününde servise devredilmiştir. Bu olgu, influenza enfeksiyonunun genç ve immünkompetan bireylerde hızlı ilerleyen ağır pnömoni ve ARDS tablosuna neden olabileceğini ve erken tanı ile uygun yoğun bakım yönetiminin önemini göstermektedir.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Bu bulgular, genç ve immünkompetan bireylerde influenza enfeksiyonunun ciddi komplikasyonlara yol açabileceği konusunda dikkat çeker. Bu, ARDS tanısında erken tanı ve yoğun bakım stratejilerinin kritik önemini ortaya koymaktadır.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Bu olgu sunumu, tek bir hasta üzerine yapılmış olup, genelize edilebilirlik sınırlıdır. Ancak, influenza A(H3N2) ile ARDS arasındaki ilişkiye dair önemli bir gözleme dayanmaktadır.

title_zh: 青年患者流感相关ARDS管理:从诊断到治疗的多学科方法
source_body_en: İnfluenza enfeksiyonu çoğunlukla kendini sınırlayan üst solunum yolu enfeksiyonu şeklinde seyretmekle birlikte, nadiren ağır viral pnömoniye ve akut respiratuvar distres sendromuna (ARDS) yol açabilmektedir. Bu olgu sunumunda, altta yatan komorbiditesi bulunmayan 20 yaşındaki erkek hastada influenza A enfeksiyonuna sekonder, saatler içerisinde gelişen ağır ARDS tablosu ve yoğun bakım yönetimi sunulmuştur. Üst solunum yolu enfeksiyonu semptomları ile ilk başvurusunda belirgin patoloji saptanmayan hasta, yaklaşık 12 saat sonra ciddi dispne ve hipoksemi ile tekrar başvurmuş, acilde çekilen toraks BT’de bilateral yaygın buzlu cam ve konsolidasyon alanları izlenmiştir. Viral pnömoniye sekonder gelişen ağır ARDS nedeniyle hasta elektif olarak entübe edilerek yoğun bakım ünitesine alınmış ve akciğer koruyucu mekanik ventilasyon stratejileri uygulanmıştır. Solunum yolu örneklerinden yapılan polimeraz zincir reaksiyonu (PCR) testinde İnfluenza A(H3N2) saptanmıştır. Yoğun bakım izlemi sırasında oksijenizasyonu ve radyolojik bulguları hızla düzelen hasta yatışının beşinci gününde ekstübe edilmiş ve yedinci gününde servise devredilmiştir. Bu olgu, influenza enfeksiyonunun genç ve immünkompetan bireylerde hızlı ilerleyen ağır pnömoni ve ARDS tablosuna neden olabileceğini ve erken tanı ile uygun yoğun bakım yönetiminin önemini göstermektedir.
abstract_zh: 流感感染通常表现为自限性上呼吸道感染,但罕见情况下可导致严重病毒性肺炎和急性呼吸窘迫综合征(ARDS)。本病例报告中,一名无基础合并症的20岁男性患者因流感A感染继发ARDS,并在数小时内进展至重症,其诊疗及重症监护管理过程如下。患者初次就诊时仅表现为上呼吸道感染症状,未发现明显病理改变;约12小时后因严重呼吸困难和低氧血症再次就诊,胸部CT显示双侧广泛磨玻璃影及实变区域。因继发于病毒性肺炎的重症ARDS,患者择期行气管插管并收入重症监护病房,采用肺保护性机械通气策略。呼吸道标本PCR检测确认流感病毒甲型H3N2流感病毒感染。重症监护期间,患者氧合指数及影像学表现迅速改善,于入院第5天拔管,第7天转出至普通病房。本病例提示,流感感染可在年轻免疫功能正常个体中迅速进展为重症肺炎及ARDS,强调早期诊断与适当重症监护管理的重要性。

title: Targeted degradation of Influenza a virus nucleoprotein via aptamer-based PROTACs for antiviral therapy
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) poses a serious threat to public health due to its high mutability and rapid transmissibility. The viral nucleoprotein (NP), a highly conserved and essential component, has emerged as an ideal target for antiviral therapies. However, its biological function has proven challenging to modulate with conventional drugs, and no NP-targeting therapeutics have reached the market so far. Here, we report the development and application of an aptamer-based proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) for the targeted degradation of IAV NP. Utilizing the Direct-to-Biology (D2B) platform, we efficiently screened and identified NP-PROTAC#4 as a functional candidate. Subsequently, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation of NP‐PROTAC#4 (LNP@NP‐PROTAC#4) for effective intracellular delivery. Importantly, LNP@NP-PROTAC#4 demonstrated potent antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, NP-PROTAC#4 exerts its antiviral effects by targeting and degrading NP via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In conclusion, our findings provide the first evidence that NP-targeted PROTAC degrader exhibits therapeutic effects, proposing a novel therapeutic strategy for IAV.

title: Functional mapping of IFITM3 resolves its antiviral core and deciphers human influenza susceptibility
abstract: Genetic variation in interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) contributes to inter-individual differences in influenza outcome, yet a comprehensive functional map of IFITM3 variation remains unavailable. Here we show a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants across three influenza A strains using deep mutational scanning. Our data reveals a functionally constrained central region, providing functional evidence consistent with a Type II membrane topology and highlighting structural features associated with antiviral activity. Comparison with AlphaMissense reveals systematic limitations in predicting the effects of variants within unstructured N-terminal motifs and lipid-embedded domains. Crucially, computational models fail to recognize variants with enhanced antiviral activity, such as G133Q. By integrating this atlas with ClinVar and gnomAD, we provide a functional readout for rare human alleles that may influence susceptibility to infection. These findings provide a resource for interpreting human variation and establish a framework for studying host-directed antiviral mechanisms. This study generates a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants using deep mutational scanning. The resulting map resolves the protein’s intramembrane antiviral core and identifies key rare human alleles that dictate susceptibility to influenza infection
